Technology stocks were higher on Wednesday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 adding almost 0.7% in value while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (^SOX) also was rising nearly 0.7%.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
(+) Bilibili ( BILI ) was up almost 9% higher Wednesday afternoon after the online entertainment platform said it received a $317.6 million investment from Chinese internet company Tencent. Under terms of the proposed transaction, Tencent will subscribe for nearly 25.1 million new class Z Bilibili shares at $12.67 each. After the deal closes, Tencent will have a 12.3% ownership stake in Bilibili.
In other sector news:
(+) Ultralife ( ULBI ) was almost 3% higher in afternoon trading, but giving back most of its earlier gains, after the the communications equipment company announced a $10.9 million contract to supply Thales Defense & Security with vehicle amplifier-adaptors and mounted power amplifiers for use in the U.S. Army's network modernization efforts. Shipments are expected to begin before the end of the year and continue throughout 2019.
(+) Intelsat SA ( I ) climbed to a new, all-time high, rising more than 8%, after the satellite communication company said its Intelsat Jackson Holdings unit priced a $700 million private placement of 8.5% senior notes due 2024 at 100.75% of par plus accrued interest since Sept. 19. The wholly owned subsidiary expects to use net proceeds to redeem all of the remaining 7.5% senior notes due 2021 that were not redeemed using the proceeds of the parent company's private placement of 8.5% senior notes due 2024 on Sept. 19.
